newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: SOCCER-EVANGELICAL MEETINGS, SOCCER SCHOOL BAR EL SALVADOR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EVANGELICAL MEETINGS, SOCCER SCHOOL BAR EL SALVADOR.

text.p: El Salvador's national team were forced on Wednesday to look for an alternative venue to prepare for a crucial World Cup qualifier because the one they had chosen is to be used for a evangelical meeting.
The national team, returning from a three-match tour abroad, arrived at the Flor Blanca stadium to train on Wednesday but were not allowed in because it was already being used by a soccer academy.

They were then told it would also be closed for the next three days because evangelical groups were holding meetings there, prompting team captain Mauricio Cienfuegos to criticise soccer officials for poor organisation.
El Salvador, who played in the 1970 and 1982 World Cup tournaments, face Cuba at home on Sunday in group two of the semi-final stage of the CONCACAF World Cup qualifiers.
A win will take them through to the final six-team round of the CONCACAF World Cup qualifiers, for which Mexico, Jamaica and Canada have already qualified.
